primary_sources.fact: The pinned Query constructor does not consume an AbortSignal. Passing signal to query does not make it cancelable.
primary_sources.evidence: source inspection and live probe

primary_sources.fact: For a dispatched nonpipeline query, query_timeout delivers a client error without canceling the server query. The pipeline branch instead destroys the stream.
primary_sources.evidence: source inspection and live nonpipeline probe

primary_sources.fact: The pool connection timeout removes the pending acquire from its queue. Pool.connect does not accept an AbortSignal.
primary_sources.evidence: source inspection and live full-pool probe

primary_sources.fact: The pooled client release wrapper rejects duplicate release; a truthy release argument removes the connection. Application abort and finally handlers need shared ownership.
primary_sources.evidence: source inspection, live discard probe, scratch ownership assertions

primary_sources.fact: release(true) returns void. Pool removal emits remove from the client.end completion callback; a listener must be registered before retirement and match the owned client.
primary_sources.evidence: source inspection; live probe observed removal and backend absence but did not implement a general retirement helper

primary_sources.fact: Transactions require a single checked-out connection, pool.end drains the pool, and release(true) discards a client.
primary_sources.evidence: official documentation

primary_sources.fact: AbortSignal is notification for APIs that support it; an already-aborted signal must be checked. Once-only listeners still require removal on normal completion.
primary_sources.evidence: official documentation and scratch ownership assertions

primary_sources.fact: For cancellation during an active operation, the pinned async driver attempts cancellation with a five-second allowance and then waits up to a further five seconds for the operation; failure to finish closes the connection. These are internal allowances, not a complete end-to-end deadline guarantee.
primary_sources.evidence: source inspection; only healthy local cancellation executed

primary_sources.fact: Async connection context rollback/commit is awaited; pooled connections remain owned by their pool rather than being closed as standalone context-managed connections.
primary_sources.evidence: source inspection and live transaction-context probe

primary_sources.fact: Pool.connection wraps getconn with context-managed connection use and finally putconn. Canceled waiting slots are rejected when a returned connection reaches them.
primary_sources.evidence: source inspection and live size-one pool probe

primary_sources.fact: Pool reset accepts idle connections, rolls back open/failed transactions, and closes active or unresettable connections.
primary_sources.evidence: source inspection

primary_sources.fact: wait_for waits for cancellation completion; timeout expiration does not imply cleanup has already finished.
primary_sources.evidence: official documentation and separate native runtime probe

primary_sources.fact: A successful cancellation dispatch does not establish the outcome of the target command; the command may already have finished.
primary_sources.evidence: official documentation; COMMIT response loss verified separately in storage-probe-results.json

primary_sources.fact: statement_timeout is a server-side statement budget; zero disables it. It does not by itself implement a complete request or transaction budget.
primary_sources.evidence: official documentation; positive local limits used in probes

primary_sources.fact: Pool.BeginTx uses the context for acquisition and BEGIN, but cancellation does not automatically roll back the returned transaction; Commit or Rollback remains required.
primary_sources.evidence: source inspection; see matching observations and limitations

primary_sources.fact: Real-transaction Rollback marks the transaction closed. If ROLLBACK execution fails, pgx kills the connection. A second Rollback sees ErrTxClosed; it cannot repair the same failed transaction.
primary_sources.evidence: source inspection; see matching observations and limitations

primary_sources.fact: The pool transaction wrapper releases its connection after Commit or Rollback, including error returns.
primary_sources.evidence: source inspection; see matching observations and limitations

primary_sources.fact: Pool connection Release destroys a closed, busy, or non-idle-transaction connection instead of returning it as reusable idle capacity.
primary_sources.evidence: source inspection; see matching observations and limitations

primary_sources.fact: The default watcher sets an immediate socket deadline on cancellation. Most canceled in-flight operations return promptly and close their connection; server CancelRequest-only behavior requires a different configuration.
primary_sources.evidence: source inspection; see matching observations and limitations

primary_sources.fact: A closed connection may still own network resources. asyncClose sends a cancellation, drains, and closes in a background task with an internal 15-second deadline; CleanupDone closes when those resources finish.
primary_sources.evidence: source inspection; see matching observations and limitations

primary_sources.fact: The pool destructor gives connection close/CleanupDone a 15-second background allowance, independent of the request context.
primary_sources.evidence: source inspection; see matching observations and limitations

primary_sources.fact: Pool.Acquire delegates to puddle; a full pool waits on a context-aware semaphore and returns the context error on cancellation.
primary_sources.evidence: source inspection; see matching observations and limitations

primary_sources.fact: Canceling an acquisition that has begun connection construction does not cancel construction. Puddle owns and returns a late successful connection to its pool. pgxpool supplies a default two-minute ConnectTimeout when none is configured. This differs from cancellation while the pool is full.
primary_sources.evidence: source inspection; see matching observations and limitations

primary_sources.fact: BeginTxFunc also reuses its supplied context for BEGIN, ROLLBACK, and COMMIT; it does not create an independent cleanup budget.
primary_sources.evidence: source inspection; see matching observations and limitations

portable_acceptance_contract.requirement: A single owner retains the acquisition promise, connection, transaction, query, and cleanup tasks until completion or explicit handoff. Canceling the public request must not abandon their ownership.
portable_acceptance_contract.counterexample: Promise.race returns abort while pool.connect later hands out an unreleased client.
portable_acceptance_contract.verification: Late-acquire ownership assertion; live full-pool race; final pool capacity and session checks.

portable_acceptance_contract.requirement: Track not-dispatched, transaction-active, commit-dispatched, and commit-acknowledged phases independently from request cancellation. A transport error or discard after commit dispatch remains unknown unless authoritative evidence resolves it.
portable_acceptance_contract.counterexample: release(true), CancelledError, or context.Canceled after COMMIT dispatch is labeled rollback despite a potentially committed write.
portable_acceptance_contract.verification: Reuse prior COMMIT-response-suppression test for the final API in each language; not repeated in this research.

portable_acceptance_contract.requirement: Return a connection only after acknowledged transaction finalization and usable protocol state; otherwise discard it and await owned cleanup.
portable_acceptance_contract.counterexample: Node query_timeout settles while SQL keeps running; next borrower inherits the unfinished transaction or query.
portable_acceptance_contract.verification: Size-one pool cancellation, fresh request, final sessions, and driver-specific idle/cleanup signals.

portable_acceptance_contract.requirement: Give acquisition and SQL finite budgets and reserve shutdown capacity for cleanup. Cleanup may outlast the request timeout. Positive remaining SQL budgets must never accidentally become zero, which disables statement_timeout.
portable_acceptance_contract.counterexample: An already-canceled request context is reused for rollback; a timed-out response is reported as all work stopped.
portable_acceptance_contract.verification: Fresh Go cleanup context, Python cleanup overrun demonstration, owned tasks joined, source-inspected internal cleanup allowances.

portable_acceptance_contract.requirement: Recover unknown outcomes using the same authenticated tenant, fixed namespace, request key, and validated intent within the retained reservation protocol.
portable_acceptance_contract.counterexample: A fresh key, changed tenant, expired record, changed payload, or external nontransactional effect defeats the same-key guarantee.
portable_acceptance_contract.verification: Shared contract and prior storage probe; final language implementations remain future work.

typescript: Use a finite connectionTimeoutMillis; check AbortSignal before acquire and immediately after awaited acquire. Release any late client before propagating cancellation. No acquisition listener is needed when owner deliberately waits for bounded acquire settlement.
Keep pipeline disabled for the initial example. Do not pass an invented query signal or mistake query_timeout for server cancellation.

On a checked-out lease, install an idempotent abort handler, then recheck signal.aborted. Share a release/discard gate with finally; remove the listener on success, failure, and cancellation. Check cancellation again before dispatching SQL.
On active cancellation, documented release(true) can retire the connection; still await the owned query and cleanup path. Server-side deadlines limit work continuing after socket teardown.

Awaiting release(true) does not join cleanup because it returns void. A completion helper can register an exact-client pool remove listener before retirement and remove it on settlement; this helper shape is source-derived, not implemented in the scratch model.
If public response cancellation must be immediate, keep a supervised cleanup promise and join it during drain; this alternative was not implemented or tested here.
python: Open and await readiness of one application-owned AsyncConnectionPool. Use one checked-out connection for each concurrent transaction; the scratch path uses autocommit=True plus an explicit transaction context.
Let CancelledError propagate through awaited transaction and pool context exits. Cancel and then await owned tasks; do not convert cancellation into a successful return.
Budget for the pinned driver cancellation/drain allowances. The observed healthy 11 ms cleanup is not a network-failure guarantee.

If a transaction context implicitly commits on exit, record the commit-dispatch boundary conservatively before that exit and retain unknown outcome on cancellation there. Exact phase instrumentation remains final-implementation work.
go: Pass the request context to acquisition, BEGIN, statements, and COMMIT. Beginning a transaction does not create automatic rollback on later context cancellation.
Create context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), cleanupBudget) inside deferred rollback, call its cancel function, and preserve primary request errors separately from cleanup errors.
Do not first call Rollback with the canceled request context and then try again with a fresh context: the first failed rollback closes the transaction.
When default in-flight cancellation already retired the connection, fresh rollback cannot repair it. Join application goroutines and observe CleanupDone or the pool shutdown boundary as appropriate.
Configure connection construction timeout separately; canceled acquisition can leave pool-owned construction running. This construction case was source-inspected only.

cleanup_safeguards: Do not delete native cancellation propagation, late-acquisition ownership, exact-once release, listener disposal, transaction context exits, fresh cleanup contexts, owned task joins, or COMMIT phase tracking as apparent duplication.
Do not replace explicit rollback with unconditional release, combine awaited work into fire-and-forget callbacks, or replace server statement deadlines with client-only query timeouts.
Cleanup acceptance must preserve the same mutation, result, cancellation, and resource observations; lower line count alone is insufficient.

execution.assertion_note: The seven ownership-model cases contain explicit assertions. Live driver fixtures record outcomes and exit after execution; their captured observations were inspected against the acceptance questions. Do not describe every recorded field as a separate assertion or a complete final-API test.

limitations: One local PostgreSQL instance and one released driver version per language; no TLS, proxies, failover, network partition, process crash, restore, power loss, replication, or external-system atomicity tests.
Synthetic mutations isolate cancellation and pool ownership. The complete inventory reservation service and its equivalent language behavior have not been implemented by these probes.
COMMIT-phase cancellation/response loss was not repeated. storage-probe-results.json is separate synchronous Python evidence, not native TypeScript/Go/Python-async COMMIT coverage.
No repeated cancellation during cleanup, hostile listener interference, Node pipeline mode, custom pgx cancellation watcher, or production HTTP disconnect adapter was exercised.
Go connection construction continuing after acquisition cancellation and driver internal cleanup deadlines are source-only findings, not fault-injected timing guarantees.
Timings are local observations from a handful of cases and are not performance targets. Resource counts after completion do not prove every cancellation schedule is leak-free.

Package lock and Go sums remain in the named scratch directory; published JSON includes hashes and pins. Final runnable examples must carry their own locked dependencies and repeat their acceptance tests.
